title: The School of Life: An Emotional Education

audiences: Readers seeking a humane introduction to self-knowledge, emotional maturity, love, work, and the uses of culture
People who find clinical psychology too technical but want more depth than slogan-based self-help
Readers questioning romantic ideals about instinct, perfect partners, vocation, success, or happiness
People willing to use philosophy, art, and psychotherapy as prompts for reflection rather than as settled science

sources.supports: Institutional description, topics, intended reader benefit, paperback format, and page count.

sources.title: The School of Life: An Emotional Education
sources.author_or_publisher: The School of Life; FlipHTML5 host
sources.supports: Full-book structure and detailed coverage of Self, Others, Relationships, Work, and Culture; title page identifies the work as introduced by Alain de Botton.

sources.title: Emotional Education: An Introduction
sources.supports: The wider project: emotional skills can be taught, modern education neglects them, and useful self-help can draw on culture without academic language.
sources.limitations: Institutional essay closely aligned with the book, not independent validation.

sources.title: The School of Life: An Emotional Education — review
sources.supports: Independent assessment of authorship, eighteen acknowledged contributors, smooth curation, practical lessons, accessibility, strongest arguments, and the view that it is engaging but not de Botton's best work.
sources.limitations: Single trade review and not an empirical evidence audit.

sources.title: The School of Life Preaches Pessimism over Romanticism
sources.supports: Independent reading of the anti-Romantic argument, careful curation, self-help orientation, diagnostic value, and lack of philosophical depth or a full treatment plan.
sources.limitations: Philosophy magazine review rather than peer-reviewed criticism.

sources.title: Book Review: The School of Life — An Emotional Education
sources.supports: Independent praise for worthy insights and criticism that the formal, broad presentation can bury its strongest material.
sources.limitations: General-interest review with limited evidence analysis.

sources.title: The School of Life: An Emotional Education
sources.supports: Large-scale reader reception and recurring praise for warmth and quotable insight alongside criticism of repetition, obvious advice, and breadth.
sources.limitations: Self-selected, mutable ratings across editions; not used in the content score.

sources.title: Reviews — The School of Life, An Emotional Education
sources.supports: A second reader aggregate, including the balance of high average approval with some non-completion and comments on accessibility, pragmatism, and note-taking value.
sources.limitations: Self-selected and mutable; editions and reviewer expertise are uncontrolled.

sources.title: Emotional Intelligence: An Integrative Meta-Analysis and Cascading Model
sources.author_or_publisher: Dana L. Joseph and Daniel A. Newman; Journal of Applied Psychology
sources.supports: The need to distinguish ability emotional intelligence from mixed models that overlap with personality and self-perception.
sources.limitations: Work-performance meta-analysis, not a direct test of this book's curriculum.

sources.title: The Impact of Enhancing Students' Social and Emotional Learning: A Meta-Analysis of School-Based Universal Interventions
sources.author_or_publisher: Joseph Durlak et al.; Child Development, indexed by the Office of Justice Programs
sources.supports: Broad evidence from 213 school programmes that structured social and emotional skills can be taught and can improve several student outcomes.
sources.limitations: School-age programmes with defined curricula; does not validate this adult anthology or every claim in it.

sources.title: Intergenerational transmission of parent-child relationship qualities to adult romantic relationships: A systematic review
sources.author_or_publisher: Mengya Xia et al.; Marriage & Family Review, indexed by PubMed
sources.supports: Evidence that parent-child attachment and interaction quality can be associated with later romantic relationship functioning.
sources.limitations: Forty dyadic studies with varied measures; mechanisms, context, and gender matter, so the evidence does not justify a simple deterministic script.

sources.title: Childhood Emotional Maltreatment and Romantic Relationships: A Meta-Analysis
sources.author_or_publisher: Emily K. Fitzgerald and colleagues; Trauma, Violence, & Abuse
sources.supports: A modest association between childhood emotional maltreatment and poorer adult romantic relationship well-being.
sources.limitations: The average association is small and weaker in more rigorous studies; it cannot establish an inevitable adult pattern for an individual.

sources.title: Psychodynamic therapy and cognitive-behavioral therapy in the treatment of depressive disorders: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
sources.author_or_publisher: American Psychological Association; indexed by PubMed
sources.supports: Evidence that manualised psychodynamic therapy can perform similarly to manualised cognitive behavioural therapy for adult depressive disorders.
sources.limitations: Treatment-specific evidence for depression; it neither validates informal introspection nor makes psychotherapy universally suitable.

sources.title: Where to get urgent help for mental health
sources.supports: Counterevidence to any romantic reading of breakdown: severe distress or danger can require urgent professional help.
sources.limitations: UK service guidance, not a scholarly analysis of the book's language.

workflow.coverage_notes: The complete book was reviewed through a readable third-party copy and cross-checked against the Penguin sample, two library catalogues, the collective author's pages, three independent reviews, two reader aggregates, five specialist evidence sources, and NHS crisis guidance. The third-party copy's edition provenance is uncertain, so exact metadata comes from publisher and catalogue records.
